checkpoint_scope: Two source-compiled programs, two pending atomic calls, before and after recorded dispatch. Old VM, IR, catalog and owning scope are dropped; only a closed weak lease survives for stale-owner rejection. New hosts rebuild original return-site paths, captures and prepared operands with the exact remaining fuel.
receipt_scope: A trusted host ledger deduplicates recorded settled calls and caches terminal outcomes. Reopening the same completed checkpoint leaves ledger bytes unchanged. No claim covers a crash after an external effect but before its receipt write.
correspondence_scope: Candidate bytes must match the trusted committed fixture image before decoding or reconstruction. Each of eight paths rejects ten altered top-level fields, truncated JSON and an oversized candidate. This is correspondence, not authentication of storage, nor validation of arbitrary malicious committed records.
authority_scope: Eight paths reject each of entry-admission denial and revocation after VM restoration but before prepared-call restoration/cached receipt use. Original closed-scope replies preserve their input and remaining fuel when refused.
ownership_scope: Storage format, host-native value codecs, state loading, receipt settlement and deduplication are fixture adapter policy. Original LocalVm, PreparedCall, return stack, evaluator and fuel implementation are reused. Serde dependencies are dev-only on the VM.
verification_scope: Local macOS same-process disk reopen. Four Rust tests contain the matrix iterations; package and consumer runs overlap and are not unique-test totals. No Linux, real GUI, subprocess restart, production journal, storage authenticity or power-loss acceptance.
remaining_boundaries: General composed helper/group checkpoint ownership and acceptance.
Process restart and external-effect crash consistency under an explicit host storage contract.
Final independent repository and distribution acceptance.
